text:
Ravi: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC draft review: need to settle on artifact GC semantics when bundles reference shared blobs (models referenced by multiple bundles).
Maya: agree. naive LRU could evict shared blob still needed by an older approved bundle. we need reference counting or ref-graph.
Theo: propose using a reference manifest per catalog that maps blob -> set(bundle_id:group_id). GC only removes blobs with empty refset and not pinned.
Ravi: how do we handle stale refs when operator deletes a bundle? must ensure atomic update to manifest and blob removal.
Maya: update workflow: import -> validate -> write blobs to staging -> compute new manifest -> atomically swap manifest file -> GC worker sees old manifest replaced and removes blobs not in new manifest.
Theo: implement manifest as content-addressed file + a symlink `current-manifest` updated with atomic rename. GC reads current-manifest, compares to local store.
security-bot: ensure manifest updates are signed so we can prove who wrote the manifest.
Ravi: edge-case: partially applied import that died during manifest swap. propose write temp-manifest, fsync, then rename into place; if crash occurs, GC will see temp files and leave blobs until next successful swap.
Maya: retention policy config example:
```yaml
gc:
  keep_unreferenced_for: 168h # grace period
  pin_labels: ["production", "pinned"]
  max_local_storage_gb: 1024
  eviction_policy: refcount-first-then-lru
```
Theo: node-side verifier should consult manifest to know expected blob locations and check digests before activation.
Ravi: question: do we allow lazy-pull of missing blobs during activation? for airgap maybe not. default: activation fails if blobs missing; operator can trigger fetch from import dir.
Maya: we should provide an `staged-fetch` CLI that tries to copy missing blobs from adjacent caches (usb, seed cache) and reports progress.
deploy-bot: started staging job on canary cluster for manifest v2.3.1 :white_check_mark:
Theo: next action: add manifest swap atomicity section to the RFC and a small test harness that simulates crashes during swap.
Ravi: i'll own the GC worker PoC. Maya and Theo will pair on atomic swap tests.
Maya: will also add metrics for orphaned bytes and time-to-gc for alerting.
